statements.paraphrase: Diraq's case is the foundry: qubits made like phone chips, a route to millions on one chip; its eight-qubit system enters Equinix Sydney in October 2026.

statements.machine: HRL exchange-only silicon spin processor (18 EO qubits from 54 quantum dots)
statements.quote: HRL's approach addresses a central obstacle for all quantum computing platforms: how to control the enormous number of qubits that a useful machine will require without an unmanageable tangle of wiring and electronics.
statements.paraphrase: HRL puts a cryogenic CMOS controller beside its exchange-only spin qubits to avoid a wiring tangle; it ran error correction on 18-qubit devices without room-temperature input.

statements.quote: prototype silicon quantum computers implementing quantum error-correcting codes at the 100-qubit scale in fiscal 2028 and at the 1,000-qubit scale in fiscal 2030
statements.paraphrase: Hitachi, with Intel and AIST, plans error-corrected silicon prototypes of 100 qubits in fiscal 2028 and 1,000 in fiscal 2030, using Intel 18A to cut device-to-device variation.

statements.quote: Built using standard semiconductor processes, allowing it to scale on the cadence of global chip progress.
statements.paraphrase: Equal1's RacQ, successor to Bell-1, is a silicon-spin computer cooled to 0.3 K inside a standard 19-inch rack, meant to scale with ordinary chip progress.

statements.quote: The system has a data-centre-friendly footprint of just three 19" server racks, housing the dilution refrigerator and integrated control electronics.
statements.paraphrase: Quantum Motion delivered QM-One, a full-stack computer on a standard CMOS process, to the UK NQCC in three server racks, and promises commercially useful machines this decade.

statements.quote: 2033 → Universal, fault-tolerant quantum computers
statements.paraphrase: SQC's site dates universal, fault-tolerant quantum computers to 2033; it gives no qubit number.

statements.quote: What you scale, matters. Our quantum processors only contain two types of atoms: silicon (14) and phosphorus (15).
statements.paraphrase: SQC builds only from silicon and phosphorus atoms and says this simplicity gives a superior reduction in bit-flip errors.

statements.quote: SQC's architecture demonstrates the opposite: as qubit count increases, the qubit quality strengthens – a critical requirement for fault tolerant, commercial scale systems.
statements.paraphrase: SQC places phosphorus atoms in pure silicon to 0.13 nm and claims its qubits improve rather than degrade as more are added.

statements.quote: By entangling all combinations of local and non-local nuclear-spin pairs, we map out the performance of the processor and achieve state-of-the-art Bell-state fidelities of up to 99.5%.
statements.paraphrase: The 11-qubit processor, two multi-atom registers, reached Bell-state fidelities up to 99.5% on both local and non-local nuclear-spin pairs.

statements.quote: develop a detailed research and development roadmap through to 2033. This will include technical requirements and highly detailed designs.
statements.paraphrase: Selected for Stage B of DARPA's Quantum Benchmarking Initiative, SQC is to write a detailed R&D roadmap and designs for a utility-scale machine by 2033.

statements.paraphrase: Fujitsu and TU Delft/QuTech built a working diamond-spin prototype with tin-vacancy centres on photonic chips, run from Fujitsu's hybrid platform; no qubit count is given.

statements.paraphrase: Fujitsu plans a multi-module diamond-spin prototype by 2027, citing high fidelity and optical links between modules as the reason for the modular route.

statements.quote: DARPA will have full access to our latest topological system on site.
statements.paraphrase: Microsoft opened a quantum research centre in Maryland where DARPA gets full on-site access to its Majorana 2 system for independent testing.

statements.quote: Based on this rapid progress, we are accelerating our roadmap to a scalable, practical quantum computer—we have cut our timeline in half and now aim to reach this target by 2029.
statements.paraphrase: After Majorana 2, Microsoft says it halved its timeline and aims at a scalable, practical quantum computer by 2029; no qubit count is attached to the date.

statements.quote: Further time-resolved measurements reveal a characteristic parity switching time of ∼ 20 s with some instances reaching minute-scale.
statements.paraphrase: With lead replacing aluminium, Microsoft reports a parity lifetime near 20 s, some a minute, measured on one nanowire of a tetron in a multi-tetron array; not yet peer-reviewed.

statements.quote: Topological qubits are uniquely suited to this task due to their inherently low error rates, small size, and digital control.
statements.paraphrase: Microsoft's reason for Majorana qubits: protection in the hardware gives low error rates, the qubits are small, and they are controlled digitally by measurement.

statements.quote: This new architecture used to develop the Majorana 1 processor offers a clear path to fit a million qubits on a single chip that can fit in the palm of one's hand.
statements.paraphrase: Microsoft presented Majorana 1 as eight topological qubits on a chip designed to scale to one million, with measurements switched by voltage pulses.

statements.paraphrase: D-Wave plans Advantage3 as a multi-chip annealer: 20,000 qubits in 2029 and 100,000 by 2031.

statements.quote: D-Wave annealing quantum computer performs magnetic materials simulation in minutes that would take nearly one million years and more than the world's annual electricity consumption to solve using a classical supercomputer
statements.paraphrase: D-Wave says an Advantage2 prototype simulated magnetic-material dynamics in minutes where a classical supercomputer would need nearly a million years; the result is published in Science.

statements.paraphrase: Quantinuum says its Helix code, concatenated high-rate blocks run on Helios, depends on moving ions: fixed wiring could not provide the connections it needs.

statements.paraphrase: Quantinuum's reason for transport: moving ions lets any qubit meet any other, which it says opens codes and algorithms that fixed layouts cannot run.

statements.quote: Individual iQPUs are then connected using UQConnect (record-breaking chip link technology) to naturally scale to millions of qubits.
statements.paraphrase: Universal Quantum joins trap-chip modules by moving ions from one chip to the next, which it says scales naturally to millions of qubits.

statements.org: Lebedev Physical Institute (FIAN) and Russian Quantum Center (Rosatom)
statements.quote: Планарные ловушки позволяют перейти от работы с единой цепочкой ионов к более сложным конфигурациям из нескольких небольших массивов, ионы между которыми можно перемещать.
statements.paraphrase: The Russian ion groups moved to planar traps: several small arrays with ions shuttled between them replace the single chain; so far trapping, transport and single-qubit gates.

statements.quote: Today, we unveil the LYNX Series, a new generation of 19-inch rack-mounted quantum computers that has officially achieved a record-breaking Quantum Volume (QV) of 32768.
statements.paraphrase: AQT claims quantum volume 32,768 for LYNX, a rack-mounted chain machine needing no cryogenics; first units go to strategic partners in Q4 2026.

statements.quote: Scaling quantum computation beyond the limits of a single chip is essential for realizing a future quantum internet.
statements.paraphrase: IonQ entangled two of its commercial trapped-ion computers through photons and presents such links as its route past a single chip; no rate or fidelity given.

statements.quote: In our Tempo development system, this was achieved in a single ion chain with all-to-all connectivity.
statements.paraphrase: IonQ reports #AQ 64 on a Tempo development system, three months early, with all 64 qubits in one all-to-all chain.

statements.quote: This will be followed in 2027 by the Perspective series, featuring 1,000 physical qubits and up to 100 logical qubits.
statements.paraphrase: Quantum Art cuts long chains into cores with laser-defined boundaries; it plans Perspective, 1,000 physical and 100 logical qubits, in 2027 and a million physical by 2033.

statements.quote: Мы показали, что можем очень дешево с точки зрения материальных ресурсов удвоить количество кубитов в нашей системе.
statements.paraphrase: FIAN built its 50-qubit ion machine on qudits: using more than two levels per ion doubles the qubit count at little hardware cost.

items.note: Direction change inside the architecture: the Russian ion programme (FIAN, RQC) announced on 12 Aug 2026 that it is moving from the single linear chain to planar (surface-electrode) traps with ion transport between small arrays (Yb-171 at FIAN, Ca at RQC; demonstrated trapping, shuttling along the chip and single-qubit operations only; two-qubit gates not reported). FIAN's I. Zalivako: 'На сегодняшний день у меня нет сомнений, что дальнейшее развитие ионных квантовых компьютеров связано с переходом к планарным технологиям'; stated goal: reach the level of the world's leading projects 'на горизонте до 2030 года' (no qubit number). The 50-qubit machine is Yb-171-based per Strana Rosatom (20 Oct 2025, https://strana-rosatom.ru/2025/10/20/rosatom-pokazal-samyj-moshhnyj-kvant/). AQT's LYNX page gives no qubit count; its QV 32,768 (2^15) is below Quantinuum H2's 2^25 (§9 [I2]), so 'record-breaking' is a European/rack-class claim. statements.quote: The company aims to develop a working system with more than several hundred qubits and quantum error correction capabilities by fiscal year 2027.
statements.paraphrase: Yaqumo, now testing Fujitsu's STAR architecture on its ytterbium hardware, aims at a system of several hundred qubits with error correction by fiscal 2027.

statements.quote: By the end of 2027, the system is planned to operate as a quantum co-processor within LRZ's high-performance computing infrastructure.
statements.paraphrase: planqc says MAQCS, a 1,000-qubit demonstrator at TRL 5 whose first hardware reached LRZ in September 2026, will run as an LRZ co-processor by end-2027.

statements.quote: Magne is expected to come online early in 2027.
statements.paraphrase: Microsoft expects Magne, Atom Computing hardware with more than 1,200 physical qubits under Microsoft's software, online in early 2027, offering logical qubits on demand.

statements.quote: This overhead can be reduced by engineering physical qubits with fewer errors, and by shaping the residual errors to be more easily correctable.
statements.paraphrase: Princeton's case for the metastable ytterbium qubit: error correction costs too much, so bias the remaining errors toward erasures, which are cheaper to correct.

statements.quote: Atom's nuclear-spin qubits exhibit record-breaking coherence times, which are essential for running deep, complex algorithms.
statements.paraphrase: Atom Computing's reasons: ytterbium nuclear-spin qubits hold coherence longest, rearrangement gives all-to-all connectivity, and a zoned layout runs operations in parallel.

statements.quote: Today, we have shown that practical quantum error correction can be achieved with our neutral-atom technology.
statements.paraphrase: Atom Computing calls its toric-code run practical error correction: many rounds sustained, with errors falling as more qubits are used; the first on neutral atoms, it says.

items.note: Princeton statement: the Nature Physics paper (12 Jun 2026, doi 10.1038/s41567-026-03309-0) is arXiv 2506.13724 (Zhang, ..., Thompson, v1 16 Jun 2025); §9 [N8] pairs the same Nature Physics URL with arXiv 2305.05493, which is the earlier Ma et al. Nature 2023 paper — worth separating. Magne: QuNorth's page (§9 [N29]) gives '>1,200' physical and '~50' logical qubits, early 2027; the Novo Nordisk Foundation release (17 Jul 2025, §9 [N22]) says operational 'around the turn of the year 2026/27' — so the date has held; the Microsoft blog (3 Aug 2026) gives no logical count. Atom Computing Series (16 Jun 2026, https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/atom-computing-raises-more-than-300-million-to-accelerate-deployment-of-fault-tolerant-neutral-atom-quantum-computers-302800832.html, §9 [N19]) states systems with 'over 1,200 qubits' and gives no new target. Atom Computing's technology page (https://atom-computing.com/quantum-computing-technology/, undated) adds: 'The closed outer electron shell of alkaline-earth metal atoms provides insensitivity to environmental perturbations, enabling our qubits to achieve industry-leading coherence times.' planqc: the MAQCS page names neither strontium nor ytterbium; planqc's LOGIQC (selected 22 Sep 2026, §9 [N34]) is 'based on neutral ytterbium atoms', aimed at the federal goal of 'at least two error-corrected quantum computers ... by 2030', with an entry demonstration due by 31 Mar 2027 and no qubit numbers. Yaqumo also states: 'Neutral-atom quantum computers are characterized by their ease of achieving all-to-all connectivity between qubits.' Could not open: none.

statements.quote: A single hardware platform supports analog workloads today and is designed to evolve toward fault-tolerant quantum computing in the future.
statements.paraphrase: Pasqal treats analog as a present use of the same hardware it intends to make fault-tolerant, not as a separate machine line.

statements.quote: the successful application of our systems to solve complex differential equations and simulate materials beyond the practical reach of classical computing
statements.paraphrase: Pasqal's September 2026 results claim materials simulations beyond practical classical reach, citing 256 atoms on Orion Beta modelling TmMgGaO₄ against crystal measurements.

statements.quote: Here, we use a 256-qubit Rydberg simulator to implement the effective Hamiltonian of the frustrated triangular-lattice magnet TmMgGaO4.
statements.paraphrase: A 256-atom analog run reproduced the magnetization curves of a real frustrated magnet and located its antiferromagnetic transition, agreeing with crystal measurements; preprint.

statements.quote: Pasqal is developing a 250-qubit QPU specifically optimized for achieving quantum advantage (where quantum outperforms classical computers in real-world tasks) on an industry-relevant problem, targeted for demonstration in the first part of 2026.
statements.paraphrase: Pasqal promised a 250-qubit processor built for quantum advantage on an industry problem, to be demonstrated in the first part of 2026.

statements.quote: Real-time gauge-theory dynamics with dozens of qubits reach the limits of classical simulations, validating quantum hardware as a discovery tool.
statements.paraphrase: QuEra presents Aquila's string-breaking run, several dozen rubidium atoms in a kagome lattice, as dynamics at the limit of classical simulation.

statements.quote: Quantum simulation can be used to boil down very complicated systems into simpler models to then understand open questions that current computers cannot answer, such as why some materials conduct electricity without any losses even at relatively high temperatures
statements.paraphrase: ICFO built QUIONE, a strontium quantum-gas microscope, to simulate models of materials that computers cannot solve, such as high-temperature superconductors.

items.note: Quantum-advantage date: Pasqal's Jun 2025 roadmap targeted a 250-qubit QPU demonstration 'in the first part of 2026'; its 29 Jan 2026 blog (https://www.pasqal.com/blog/inside-pasqals-2026-vision-on-quantum-for-industry-and-research/) restated the objective 'before mid-2026' and named Vela ('will launch in 2026 with over 256 high-quality qubits ... the first QPU engineered for quantum advantage specifications'); the H1-2026 results (24 Sep 2026) name neither a quantum-advantage demonstration nor Vela and cite the TmMgGaO4 and differential-equation work instead — the promised demonstration was not found as announced by the 26 Sep 2026 cut-off (only Pasqal's own pages were checked). The TmMgGaO4 run is on Orion Beta, a machine the register files under atom_rb (digital primary) — analog work continues on machines filed as gate-model, which bears on §8.3.9's demotion test. arXiv 2603.20372 v1 (20 Mar 2026) was titled 'One-to-one quantum simulation of the low-dimensional frustrated quantum magnet TmMgGaO4 with 256 qubits'; the current version is shorter. QuEra (4 Jun 2025): Aquila 'arranged up to several dozen rubidium atoms in a kagome-geometry optical-tweezer lattice'; the Nature paper itself makes no advantage claim (§8.3.9). ICFO (22 Apr 2024), L. Tarruell also: 'we also expect to obtain much more computational power to use these machines as analog quantum computers' (no date or number). No renames noticed. PsiQuantum's CEO changed on 10 Feb 2026 (Victor Peng interim CEO, O'Brien executive chairman); the 22 Jul 2026 DARPA release ($125 M, Stage C) contains the line 'it now seems likely that someone will build a utility-scale quantum computer by 2033', which reads as DARPA's, not a PsiQuantum target. The Sep 2025 $1 B release (https://www.psiquantum.com/news-import/psiquantum-1b-fundraise) states: 'PsiQuantum was founded on the premise that commercially valuable quantum computing requires error correction—and therefore on the order of a million physical qubits.' statements.quote: We've cut our loss ratio dramatically, and that progress is what gives us confidence in reaching fault tolerance in 2028-2029.
statements.paraphrase: Xanadu's chief executive dates fault tolerance to 2028–29, resting the date on the reduction of photon loss.

statements.quote: Up to 200 logical qubits by 2029, scaling to up to 500 by 2030 and 1,000+ by 2031.
statements.paraphrase: Xanadu's August 2026 roadmap: up to 200 logical qubits by 2029, 500 by 2030, over 1,000 by 2031, from GKP qubits under an outer qLDPC code.

statements.quote: The roadmap targets a reduction in the Company's key loss technical indicator from 24.1x by 2026 to 1.0x by 2030.
statements.paraphrase: Xanadu's loss milestone: its key loss indicator falls from 24.1× in 2026 to 1.0× in 2030; the release does not define the indicator.

statements.quote: These states allow logic operations to be performed using deterministic, room-temperature-compatible techniques, and they are uniquely well-suited for networking across chips using standard fiber connections.
statements.paraphrase: Xanadu's reason for GKP qubits: deterministic logic at room temperature, and states that travel between chips over ordinary optical fibre.

statements.quote: The next hurdle towards a utility-scale photonic quantum computer remains clear: further reduction of optical loss will allow for higher quality GKP states suitable for fault-tolerance.
statements.paraphrase: After generating GKP states on a chip, Xanadu names optical loss as the remaining barrier to GKP states good enough for fault tolerance.

statements.quote: With this breakthrough, Aurora could in principle be scaled up to thousands of server racks and millions of qubits today, realizing the ultimate goal of a quantum data center.
statements.paraphrase: Xanadu presents Aurora's four fibre-linked racks as a modular design that could in principle grow to thousands of racks and millions of qubits.

items.note: The Aug 2026 roadmap (same URL as §9 [P9]) never defines its 'key loss technical indicator' (24.1x in 2026 → 1.0x in 2030); the release separately says loss must fall 'below the required error-correction threshold'. §8.3.11 ('Where it stands' and 'The next test') reads the indicator as 'loss 24x above threshold' — an interpretation, not Xanadu's wording. Other figures in the release: 'Fault tolerance milestone: 2028-2029'; logical error rate 'from roughly 10^-3-10^-8 in 2028 to 10^-16 by 2030'; architecture 'GKP encoding with quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes'; 'Xanadu's photonic architecture is designed to operate at room temperature, be manufactured using silicon processes and scale through modular, networked systems compatible with existing telecom infrastructure.' Aurora release (22 Jan 2025), C. Weedbrook: 'Xanadu has now solved scalability. Photonics really is the best and most natural way to both compute and network.' GKP release (4 Jun 2025) rests on the Nature paper already cited as §9 [P5]. The xanadu.ai press pages are script-rendered and returned no text; the same releases were read on PR Newswire. No successor machine to Aurora is named in the roadmap release. statements.quote: Later this year, the system will be upgraded to ORCA's next-generation PT-3 platform, delivering increased processing capability and deeper integration with classical compute environments.
statements.paraphrase: ORCA installed a PT-2 at a Japanese enterprise in under a week and schedules its upgrade to PT-3 for later in 2026.

statements.quote: The ability to control thousands of photons in programmable low-loss quantum processors pushes the experimental frontier into a regime far beyond classical tractability and opens a pathway to trillion-qumode three-dimensional cluster states and fault-tolerant photonic quantum hardware.
statements.paraphrase: USTC says Jiuzhang 4.0, 1,024 squeezed states in 8,176 modes with up to 3,050 detected photons, lies far beyond classical tractability and points toward fault-tolerant photonics.

statements.quote: Gaussian boson sampling not only serves as a prominent model for demonstrating quantum computational advantage but can also generate bosonic error-correcting codes for fault-tolerant quantum computing.
statements.paraphrase: USTC's reason to scale the sampler: the same squeezed-light machinery can prepare bosonic error-correcting codes, so the sampler doubles as a step toward fault tolerance.

statements.quote: The number of photonic qubits can be increased using optical-fiber delays, allowing each photon source to be reused multiple times – unlike matter-based systems.
statements.paraphrase: ORCA's case for time-bin photonics: fibre delay loops let one photon source serve many modes, so the machine grows in time rather than in hardware.

statements.quote: In a 24-month time frame, we'll reach quantum advantage.
statements.paraphrase: ORCA's chief executive expected quantum advantage within 24 months, from PT-3, which the company then expected on the market in early 2026.

items.note: Slip: PT-3 was expected 'to enter the market in early 2026' (TechJournal interview with CEO Richard Murray, interview held 13–14 May 2025; the page prints no publication date, 2025-05-14 is the interview date); ORCA's own 16 Jun 2026 release moves the PT-3 upgrade to 'later this year'. Murray's '24-month' quantum-advantage horizon runs to about May 2027. ORCA's Oct 2025 architecture page also says: 'Our architecture focuses directly on mitigating photon loss – the primary error in photonic systems – instead of managing the probabilistic operations typical of linear-optical approaches' (its FT route uses optical nonlinearities, i.e. a different architecture from the sampler). Jiuzhang 4.0: the arXiv v1 abstract (2508.09092, Aug 2025) claimed '> 10^42 years' on El Capitan with the MPS method against 25.6 µs per sample; the published Nature abstract (13 May 2026) drops the year figure and says results are 'rigorously validated against all current classical simulation methods'. Both Jiuzhang statements are author claims inside a peer-reviewed paper, tagged [D]; the 'far beyond classical tractability' reading remains open to classical challenge (§8.3.12). Xanadu's Borealis (2022) has no 2024–2026 builder statement; Xanadu now presents Aurora as its successor. Could not open: none.
